applies_why: The judge text returns UNDERDETERMINED for Isaiah 7:14 after noting that the challenger addressed the wording and the defender addressed the application, so it treats the single verse’s dual aspects as leaving the matter open.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. — I weighed (1) that a verse with two senses must have both stand and cannot be UNDERDETERMINED, against (2) that the judge may treat the challenger’s wording answer and defender’s application answer as separate unresolved aspects.
why: The judge marks Isaiah 7:14 UNDERDETERMINED because one side answered the virgin/young-woman wording and the other answered the prophetic application, rather than holding that a verse with two senses is not open and both senses stand.
